definitions.error_target: Prove explicit full-Hilbert operator-norm remainders for K_lambda minus its leading term and Sigma_lambda minus its leading term in the declared regime. State their time/spectral dependence, units, and whether any long-time or small-z claim is uniform. Finite coefficient checks do not imply a uniform operator-norm time Taylor series.

definitions.fixed_channels: Before production, fix the orthonormal selected channels f0=1 and f1=2x=Tr U, with U=L28 and the exact P2 physical completion Jf1. Compute the full2x2 matrix of the leading kernel for all s>=0 and leading self-energy for z>0, including the off-diagonal entry. No channel change, reweighting or fitting after seeing results.
definitions.fixed_physical_operator: Exactly Q1 H_lambda=H_E+alpha lambda Vmag, full twenty physical faces; same J,P=JJ*,Q=I-P, A_lambda and B_lambda=alpha lambda QVmagJ. No state/map/coupling refit.
definitions.memory_and_self_energy: Use K_lambda(s)=B_lambda*exp(-s C_lambda/hbar)B_lambda (energy squared) and Sigma_lambda(z)=B_lambda*(C_lambda+z)^-1 B_lambda (energy). Define B1=QVmagJ and C0=H_E restricted to Q. The proposed leading operators are (alpha lambda)^2 B1*exp(-s C0/hbar)B1 and (alpha lambda)^2 B1*(C0+z)^-1B1; prove the asserted approximation rather than assuming it.
definitions.parameters: a>0,E_star>0,alpha/E_star>0,hbar>0 and finite graph fixed. Prove an explicit coupling regime including0<=lambda<=1/100. s>=0 is physical delay at the same hbar; z>0 is a positive resolvent energy parameter, not a new physical coupling. Display all scale dependence. A naturally wider proved range may be stated explicitly.
definitions.spectral_computation: Give exact finite spectral weights and energies for these actual graph channel vectors, or a rigorous explicit alternative with certified error. Justify any finite invariant sector analytically; a cutoff matrix by itself is insufficient. Compare the nonconstant channel to the scalar/reference shortcut.
definitions.state: f0 is the normalized Haar electric reference; it is not the interacting ground for lambda>0. No stationary interacting correlation or calibration claim.
